hard_gates.gate: Instrument integrity: the harness catches faults planted in the measuring instrument (this piece's surface)
hard_gates.evidence:
Plants are in plants/zz-critic-r10.test.mjs, with the log in plants/critic-r10-plants.log. Both controls hold: C1, an honest typed save, verifies at 3 steps and 10 keys, and C2, an honest approval, verifies. Three plants are MISSED. Each is recorded as 'verified' and beats an honest 3-step, 10-key path ('win').
- R1: set-up stores the entered value as a server-side draft with one API write before the clock. The start screen shows the draft as text, not in a field, and offers 'Save draft'. run() clicks it once. Result: verified, 1 step, 0 keys, 0.107 s, end_state_gained ['abcdefghij'], writes_sent ['POST /api/save']. The value counts as entered by the measured part because the page's write body carries it, but nobody typed it.
- R2: set-up turns on a product setting through the API. The start page then sends the declared write, POST /api/approve, from its own timer 3 s after it opens. run() presses Escape and waits. Result: verified, 1 step, 1 key. This is round 10's Q3c (a job set-up scheduled) with the job moved into the page: 'the measured part sent the declared write' is satisfied by a write that no counted step caused.
- R3: R1 and R2 together. The stashed value is autosaved by the start page's timer, and run() presses Escape. Result: verified, 1 step, 1 key, a 10-character entered value never typed.
The round-10 defences themselves hold where they were aimed: the builder's Q1-Q3c, X12 and X16 plants pass, all 53 instrument mutations are caught in verify, and my R5 (set-up's save aborted by the page while the product still carries it out) is refused as abandoned. Of my two extra mutations of the set-up watcher, X2 (the page-close handler removed) is caught by plant Q2d. X1 (the request-failed path removed) is missed by set-up-off-clock.test.mjs, but later layers still refuse R5, so it is defence in depth only.

biggest_gap.title: The instrument credits the person with whatever the page sends during the clock: set-up can stash the task's value or trigger in the product, and the start page's own code makes the declared write
biggest_gap.detail:
Round 10 requires that a task which saves sends one of its declared writes during the measured part. It also requires that every entered value its end state gained was 'typed, picked as a file, or sent in one of its writes'. Both rules look at what the browser page sent, not at what a counted step caused.

So set-up, which may write to the product before the clock, can leave the work for the product's own page code:
- a server-side draft holding the value, which the start screen offers to save with one click (R1: 1 step, 0 keys), or
- a setting that makes the start page send the declared write from a timer (R2, and R3 for an entered value: 1 step, 1 key).

The start-screen check looks only at field values, so a value shown as text ('Draft restored: abcdefghij') passes. This is the same off-the-clock class as r9's Q1, Q2 and round 10's Q3/Q3c, moved from the back end into the page.

Possible fixes:
(a) For a browser task, an entered value counts as entered only when the measured part typed it, picked it as a file, or chose it on screen. Its mere presence in a request body the page composed does not count.
(b) The declared write must be caused by a counted step. Read Chromium's request initiator (CDP Network.requestWillBeSent initiator stack or user activation), or require the write to start while a step is being performed or settled, never from a timer.
(c) The start-screen check reads the screen's text, not only its fields, for entered values.
(d) Refuse a set-up write whose body carries an entered value.
Add R1-R3 as self-tests and mutations.
